claims.text: Machine-learning-guided optimization of cold-rolling reduction and rapid-annealing conditions can produce a hierarchical dual-phase microstructure in high-entropy alloys.
The optimized processing will improve yield strength by approximately 15–20% relative to conventional processing.
The optimized processing will improve Young’s modulus by approximately 15–20% relative to conventional processing.
The optimized processing will improve fracture resistance by roughly 15–20% relative to conventional processing.
The optimized processing will maintain or modestly enhance ductility.
Traditionally cast, homogenized, and thermomechanically treated HEAs typically have relatively coarse single-phase or simple duplex microstructures.
Controlled cold rolling followed by rapid annealing can stimulate partial recrystallization while retaining metastable phases.
The targeted microstructure consists of fine recrystallized grains coexisting with retained metastable regions.
The retained regions in the targeted microstructure exhibit favorable local chemical ordering.
Fine recrystallized regions increase yield strength.
Fine recrystallized regions increase Young’s modulus.
Retained metastable, non-recrystallized regions enhance fracture resistance.
Retained metastable, non-recrystallized regions enhance ductility.
A dual-phase architecture supplies synergistic deformation mechanisms that concurrently improve multiple mechanical properties.
Conventionally processed HEAs commonly exhibit trade-offs between strength, ductility, and fracture-related properties.
The proposed improvements should persist at room and moderately elevated temperatures under static and dynamic loading.
Excessive rolling reduction or prolonged annealing can eliminate the improvements by causing full recrystallization or grain coarsening.
The improvements may fail when the alloy composition makes the engineered phases unstable under service conditions.
The exact percentage improvements are sensitive to experimental variability and the machine-learning training data.
Long-term stability of the hierarchical microstructure under cyclic loading remains unconfirmed.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis grammatically assigns the roughly 15–20% improvement to yield strength, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance, whereas the predicted outcome assigns that numerical range only to yield strength and Young’s modulus and leaves the fracture-resistance increase unquantified.
